newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-FIRST WNBA COACH IS FIRED.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-FIRST WNBA COACH IS FIRED.

text.p: Linda Sharp became the first coach ever fired by the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) when she was dismissed by the Los Angeles Sparks on Wednesday.

The Sparks, off to a lackluster 4-7 start with four losses in their last five games, named assistant Julie Rousseau as interim coach. They also named former NBA star Orlando Woolridge an assistant coach.

"This was an extremely difficult decision, one that I take absolutely no joy in making," general manager Rhonda Windham said. "However, with the pending circumstances, such as the short duration of the season and the still realistic possibility of reaching the playoffs, we felt that a change was necessary at this time."
The 37-year-old Woolridge, a 13-year NBA veteran, moves down from the Sparks' front office.

"I'm really looking forward to this opportunity," he said. "I have sorely missed the camaraderie and competition since retiring from the NBA, and think that my experience as a player at the professional level will benefit the Sparks."
